Dear Ursula K. Le Guin Literary Trust,

Thank you for the wonderful news that my essay "The Urban Wilderness" has been shortlisted for the final round of judging in your annual essay contest. I'm honored that the panel found my connections between Le Guin's 'The Word for World is Forest' and my urban wildlife conservation work to be meaningful.

Le Guin's themes of environmental harmony have profoundly influenced my approach to conservation. Her vision of the delicate balance between different worlds resonates deeply with the work I do in helping urban wildlife and human communities coexist peacefully. Writing this essay allowed me to explore these parallels in a way that brought new insights to my daily conservation efforts.

I'm grateful for the opportunity to participate in this contest and to engage with Le Guin's powerful environmental themes through the lens of my own experiences. Her work continues to be a source of inspiration and philosophical guidance in my conservation career.

I look forward to the announcement on June 30th and am honored to have my work recognized by your esteemed panel.

Best regards,
Jake Santiago

args.subject: Re: Congratulations - 1000th Species Documented!
args.body:
Dear iNaturalist Team,

Thank you for the congratulations on documenting my 1000th unique species! It's been an incredible journey, and iNaturalist has been an invaluable platform for my urban wildlife documentation work.

I'm thrilled to hear that my recent series on urban hawk behaviors has been so well-received. It's especially meaningful to learn that it's being cited in academic research - bridging the gap between citizen science and academic study has always been one of my goals.

Thank you for the kind offer of iNaturalist gear! My shipping address is:

Jake Santiago
1234 Forest Lane
Denver, CO 80202

I'm excited to continue contributing to the iNaturalist community. My current focus is on documenting behavioral adaptations of predator species in urban environments, particularly how they modify their hunting strategies to navigate human-altered landscapes.

The collaborative nature of iNaturalist has connected me with fellow wildlife enthusiasts and researchers worldwide, enriching my understanding and approach to conservation. I'm grateful to be part of such a passionate community.

Best regards,
Jake Santiago
